reaction.notes:
Use this rule set ONLY if 'applies_if' tokens are present.
Evaluate base_rules top→down; if none match, use default_rule.
After choosing a rule, scan all modifiers and apply any whose 'when' tokens or symptoms match.
General guidance: form the imine/iminium efficiently (remove water or use a Lewis acid), keep pH ~5–6 for borohydrides, and avoid H2 routes when benzyl/CBz/nitro must survive.

default_rule.description: General starter: NaBH(OAc)3 (STAB) + AcOH in DCE/MeCN; good for aldehydes and many ketones.

conditions.notes: Charge carbonyl + amine first, adjust with AcOH, then add STAB portionwise.

base_rules.name: Primary amine or secondary amine to secondary/tertiary (workhorse)
base_rules.description: Broadly effective; chemoselective for iminium. Suitable for aldehydes and many ketones.

base_rules.name: Primary amine from C=O (ammonium source, cyanide-buffered)
base_rules.description: Use when forming RCH2NH2 or R2CHNH2 from carbonyls with NH4OAc/NH3; tolerant but handle cyanide risk.

conditions.notes: Avoid strong acid; add base carefully at quench.

base_rules.name: Hindered ketones, anilines, or tertiary amine targets
base_rules.description: Ti(OiPr)4 promotes imine formation/water capture; then STAB reduction.

conditions.notes: Mix carbonyl + amine + Ti(OiPr)4 (30–60 min) before adding STAB.

base_rules.name: Alternative for hindered systems (borohydride + Lewis acid)
base_rules.description: NaBH4 with Ti(OiPr)4; effective but less chemoselective—control addition and temperature.

base_rules.name: Very hindered tertiary amines
base_rules.description: BH3·THF (or BH3·SMe2) excels for secondary amine + hindered ketone → tertiary amine.

conditions.notes: Quench cautiously with MeOH at 0 °C; BH3 reduces many FGs.

base_rules.name: Catalytic hydrogenation (Pd/C)
base_rules.description: Simple and scalable for many aldimines/ketimines; avoid if benzyl/CBz/nitro must survive.

base_rules.name: Catalytic hydrogenation (Raney-Ni)
base_rules.description: Industrial option for aliphatic ketones; robust but less FG tolerant.

base_rules.name: Transfer hydrogenation (TEAF) + Pd/C
base_rules.description: Metal-catalyzed reduction without H2 cylinder; good for many aldimines.

conditions.notes: Minor N-formyl intermediates may appear and collapse under the conditions.

modifiers.suggest: Pre-mix carbonyl + amine with 3–4 Å MS or Ti(OiPr)4 (1.2–2.0 equiv) 30–60 min before adding reductant; warm to 40–60 °C if needed.
Maintain pH ≈5–6. Too acidic → cyanide risk (NaBH3CN) / over-acetylation; too basic → slow imine formation.
Avoid H2/Pd or Raney-Ni; prefer STAB/NaBH3CN/Ti(OiPr)4 routes.
Use NH4OAc/NH3 with NaBH3CN (or STAB at lower AcOH) and keep pH 5–6.
Continue heating or add mild base at workup to deprotect the formyl species.
Consider H2/Raney-Ni or H2/Pd-C if FG set allows; otherwise keep STAB and emphasize water removal.
Avoid strong acids; work in well-ventilated hood; quench carefully with base.
BH3 is reactive/pyrophoric; cool, add slowly, and quench with MeOH at 0 °C before aqueous workup.
Favor MeCN or alcohol solvents; avoid very apolar media.
Use DCE or toluene; add sieves or Ti(OiPr)4 to drive imine formation.
